---
title: "Lesson 1: What is Quarto?"
---

## Quarto in one sentence

**Quarto** is free software that turns plain-text files containing **Markdown and code** into polished documents: web pages, websites, reports (HTML, Word, PDF), and slides.

You write a `.qmd` file ("Quarto Markdown"), and Quarto **renders** it:

```
            ┌──────────────┐
 page.qmd ──►    Quarto    ├──► page.html  (web page)
 (text +    │  (+ R runs   ├──► page.docx  (Word)
  R code)   │  your code)  ├──► page.pdf   (PDF)
            └──────────────┘
```

If the file contains R code, Quarto runs it (through R's `knitr` package) and puts the results (tables, charts, numbers) into the output.

## Why use Quarto for websites?

- **Write in plain text.** No HTML or web design needed. Markdown is the same formatting you use in GitHub READMEs.
- **Code and results stay together.** A chart on the page is produced by the R code beside it, so it's reproducible.
- **Everything is version-controlled.** Pages are text files in a Git repo, so you get history, review, and collaboration (see the [Git and GitHub training](../intro-to-github/index.qmd)).
- **Free hosting.** GitHub Pages publishes the site at no cost.
- **Built-in features:** navigation, search, light and dark mode, mobile layout, copy buttons on code.

## What a Quarto website is

A **Quarto website** is a folder (a "project") containing:

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `_quarto.yml` | Site settings: title, navigation, theme, where output goes |
| `index.qmd` | The home page |
| Other `.qmd` files | The other pages |
| `styles.css` | Optional style tweaks |
| `docs/` (or `_site/`) | The **rendered website**, generated by Quarto. Never edit by hand |

You edit the `.qmd` files and `_quarto.yml`, run **render**, and Quarto rebuilds the HTML in `docs/`. GitHub Pages then serves `docs/` as a website.

## How this site works

The NV OSE training site is exactly this:

```
nv-ose/training  (GitHub repo)
├── _quarto.yml               ← navbar, sidebars, theme
├── index.qmd                 ← home page
├── pages/
│   ├── intro-to-github/      ← one folder per training
│   └── intro-to-quarto-websites/
└── docs/                     ← rendered site → https://nv-ose.github.io/training/
```

By the end of this training you'll be able to build a site like it, and add to this one.

## Key vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Quarto** | The publishing software (a command-line tool, also built into editors) |
| **`.qmd` file** | A Quarto document: YAML header + Markdown + code chunks |
| **YAML** | The settings format used in the header of each page and in `_quarto.yml` |
| **Markdown** | Simple text formatting (`**bold**`, `# Heading`, `- list`) |
| **Code chunk** | A block of R (or Python) code that Quarto runs |
| **Render** | Build the output (HTML, etc.) from `.qmd` files |
| **Preview** | Render and open a live view that updates as you edit |
| **Project** | A folder with a `_quarto.yml`, such as a website |
| **GitHub Pages** | GitHub's free hosting for static websites |
